keyVerseText: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.
rootMeaning: The word καταβολή (katabolḗ) derives from the verb καταβάλλω (katabállō), meaning 'to cast down' or 'to lay down.' This etymology suggests a literal sense of 'throwing down' or 'laying a foundation,' which goes beyond the common English gloss of 'foundation' by emphasizing the deliberate act of placing or establishing something firmly. The root conveys both the physical act of setting down and the figurative sense of establishing a beginning or origin.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, καταβολή is predominantly used to denote 'the foundation,' appearing in this sense ten times among its eleven occurrences. This consistent translation highlights the word's role in describing the starting point or basis of something, such as the foundation of the world or a building. The single occurrence translated as 'conceive' (He 11:11) shows its figurative use related to the beginning of life or conception, indicating the word's semantic range from physical foundations to metaphorical beginnings.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding καταβολή as both a physical foundation and a figurative beginning enriches our grasp of biblical themes concerning God's eternal purposes and creative acts. It underscores that God's plans and promises are grounded on a firm and deliberate foundation laid from the very beginning of creation. This word reminds believers that faith rests not on shifting sands but on the secure and purposeful establishment of God's sovereign will, which is foundational to Christian hope and assurance. Moreover, recognizing the connection between foundation and conception deepens appreciation for God's role in both creation and new spiritual life.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 13:35 speaks of things 'kept secret from the foundation of the world,' using καταβολή to emphasize the original and deliberate establishment of God's plan. This word highlights that divine mysteries and promises were not afterthoughts but were laid down from the very beginning of creation. It assures believers that God's redemptive work through Christ is rooted in eternal purpose, planned and set firmly before time itself.
